_comment: The detector-first decision rule's numbers (vision/rules.py RuleConfig).
The rule answers the three reporting classes only - C1_EMPTY, C2_ACTIVE_PLAY,
C3_MAINTENANCE_NON_SPORTING - plus UNCERTAIN, which is an abstention and not a class.
play_min and small_group_max are the facility's requirement, not fits. detector/imgsz/tiles
name the model the counts come from (vision/detector.DETECTORS): yolov8n at 1280, untiled,
chosen 2026-09-19 by a detector audit run against this decision rule.
require_ball_in_play (2026-09-21, reported from use) adds that the ball has to be in
play rather than lying on the grass: a ball that persisted across the burst but moved
less than its own width does not count. Measured in ball diameters, so there is no
threshold to fit - see vision/ball.py. Inert on a single frame, and the trace says so.
require_ball and require_motion make ACTIVE_PLAY something that must be SHOWN: more than
four people AND a ball seen in one of the burst frames AND people moving. Cross-venue
ball recall was measured at 0.40 (0.06-0.89 by venue), so require_ball costs genuine
matches wherever the detector cannot see the ball - these are switches because whether
to pay that cost is a decision.
require_motion is inert while motion_play_min is null, and the verdict's trace says so on
every frame rather than letting an unfitted requirement pass silently. Every threshold
here is fitted on venue_01 camera A only and then frozen: frozen_at,
frozen_commit and tuned_on record when, from what, and on which camera. While frozen_at
is null the worker refuses to deploy this file; offline measurement still runs against
it, since measuring an unfrozen rule is how it gets frozen.
require_ball TURNED OFF 2026-09-29. Reported from use: the rule was calling real
matches C3. Measured per frame, both detector arms identical but for this switch:
require_ball true   play-recall 0.3078, worst venue 0.1111
require_ball false  play-recall 0.9957, worst venue 0.9702
and on the empty side the two arms are the SAME to four decimals - false-play 0.0000,
empty accuracy 0.9259, C3-on-empty 0.0741. The requirement bought nothing and cost 69
points of recall.
Why, exactly: per venue the rule's play-recall IS the ball-detection rate. a 35%/0.321,
does not measure whether football is being played; it measures whether yolov8n saw the
ball, which was measured at 0.40 cross-venue. A ball 20 pixels across on a floodlit pitch is a
property of the detector, not of the booking.
The facility's rule - a game has a ball in it - is not wrong; it is not observable with
this detector. require_ball_in_play stays on and stays inert on stills, and the switch
remains a switch: a detector that can see the ball would make this worth turning back on.
2026-10-20: detector, size and person confidence re-chosen on CPU cost and accuracy.
Measured with scripts/evaluate_rules.py on 848 labelled frames (10 venues, day and night,
synthetic frames left out), the rule unchanged otherwise:
yolov8n  1280  person_conf 0.25  accuracy 0.925  empty 0.958  play 0.921  0.14 s/frame
yolo11n  1280  person_conf 0.15  accuracy 0.938  empty 0.964  play 0.937  0.18 s/frame
yolo11n   960  person_conf 0.15  accuracy 0.930  empty 0.970  play 0.925  0.09 s/frame
yolo11n   640  person_conf 0.15  accuracy 0.927  empty 0.982  play 0.918  0.06 s/frame
yolo11s   960  person_conf 0.15  accuracy 0.922  empty 0.964               0.20 s/frame
False play on empty frames is 0.000 in every row. yolo11n at 960 is chosen: better than the
old setting on every class at about half the processor time per picture, which is what a
small machine needs. 1280 buys under a point for twice the time.
edge_margin (people on the touchline) is off: boundaries here are drawn tight to the lines,
and a 2% margin cut play recall from 0.92 to 0.82. Turn it on for a camera whose boundary
includes the benches. dark_luma 20: a pitch too dark to see is UNCERTAIN, not EMPTY; no
labelled frame is that dark, so it changes nothing measured.
still_max_fraction 0.10 (people standing, not playing): measured on 86 bursts of real play
with 5+ people from the venue_01 recordings (three frames a second apart, yolo11n 960), the
share of matched people who moved was at least 0.10 in every burst (2nd percentile 0.14,
median 0.74). Below 0.10 the crowd is standing - a team talk, a queue - and the minute is C3.
It needs a burst, so a single picture (the playground checks) never triggers it.
